_provenance.generated_by: Synthetic NMSZ scenario with IASP91 velocity model
_provenance.data_origin: Station coordinates from IRIS FDSN metadata (NM network, New Madrid Seismic Zone). Velocity model from IASP91 Table 1 upper crust. Synthetic scenario, not a real event.
_provenance.real_data_accession: IRIS FDSN: network=NM (synthetic scenario; real waveform download via NestGate data.iris_fetch in Phase 0+)
_provenance.notes: Station coordinates from real IRIS FDSN metadata. Vp=5.8 km/s from IASP91 upper crust layer. Acceptance criteria based on typical regional network performance.

_description: P-wave travel time inversion for earthquake source localization from public seismic data
_groundspring_question: Can we locate an earthquake source from noisy arrival-time observations?
_data_source: IRIS Web Services (free, public, no key) — https://service.iris.edu/

travel_time_model._description: 1D layered velocity model for continental crust (IASP91-simplified)
travel_time_model._reference: Kennett & Engdahl (1991) IASP91, Geophysical Journal International

test_scenario._description: Synthetic earthquake with known location, for validation of inversion
test_scenario._note: Arrival time noise of ±0.5s is realistic for automated P-wave picks

haversine_reference._description: Great-circle NY-London (WGS-84): 5570 km. Range absorbs spherical vs ellipsoidal model difference.
